questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of a flower?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Spines**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Spines** are not a component of a flower; they are modified leaves, stems, or stipules that are typically hard, pointed, and meant for protection.
 
• Flowers are reproductive structures in angiosperms (flowering plants) and typically consist of four main parts: androecium, corolla, calyx, and gynoecium.
 
• The primary role of spines is to protect the plant from herbivores and reduce water loss, especially in arid environments.
 
• Unlike the other options listed (androecium, corolla, and calyx), spines do not play a role in the reproductive process of the flower.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Androecium**

 
 
• The androecium is the collective term for the stamens in a flower. Each stamen typically consists of a filament and an anther, where pollen is produced.
 
• It is the male reproductive part of the flower.
 
 
 
• **Corolla**
 
 
• The corolla is the collective term for the petals of a flower.
 
• Petals are often brightly colored to attract pollinators.
 
 
 
• **Calyx**
 
 
• The calyx is the collective term for the sepals of a flower.
 
• Sepals are typically green and provide protection to the flower bud before it opens.
 
 
 
• **Gynoecium**
 
 
• The gynoecium is the collective term for the female reproductive parts of a flower, consisting of one or more carpels.
 
• Each carpel typically includes an ovary, style, and stigma.

questions.question: Where was the Hindu College established in the year 1791?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Benaras**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Hindu College was established in the year 1791.
 
• It was founded in the city of Benaras, which is now known as Varanasi.
 
• The institution was set up to provide Western education to Indians.
 
• It played a significant role in the Indian Renaissance and the spread of modern education in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hindu College:**

 
 
• The Hindu College in Benaras was one of the earliest institutions to provide a structured curriculum for Western-style education in India.
 
• It was founded by influential citizens of Benaras, including Raja Rammohan Roy.
 
• The college was established with the aim of imparting modern education in various fields such as science, mathematics, and the humanities.
 
• It later evolved into the Central Hindu School and eventually became a part of Banaras Hindu University (BHU).
 
 
 
• **Banaras Hindu University (BHU):**
 
 
• Established in 1916 by Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya, BHU is one of the largest residential universities in Asia.
 
• BHU offers courses in various fields including arts, science, engineering, medicine, and agriculture.
 
• The university is renowned for its research and academic excellence.
 
• It has a sprawling campus spread over 1,300 acres in Varanasi.
 
 
 
• **Raja Rammohan Roy:**
 
 
• Raja Rammohan Roy was a prominent social and educational reformer in India during the early 19th century.
 
• He is often called the "Father of the Indian Renaissance" due to his efforts in promoting modern education and social reforms.
 
• He was an advocate for the abolition of practices such as Sati and child marriage.
 
• His contributions laid the foundation for the development of modern Indian society.

questions.question: Where is the Gulf of Mannar located?

Between the south-eastern tip of India and the western coast of Sri Lanka
Between the south-eastern tip of India and the north-western coast of Sri Lanka
Between the south-eastern tip of India and the southern coast of Sri Lanka

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Between the south-eastern tip of India and the western coast of Sri Lanka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Gulf of Mannar is a large shallow bay forming part of the Laccadive Sea in the Indian Ocean.
 
• It lies between the south-eastern tip of India and the western coast of Sri Lanka, specifically between Tamil Nadu and the Northern Province of Sri Lanka.
 
• The Gulf of Mannar is renowned for its rich biodiversity and is home to the Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park, which is one of the richest coastal regions in Asia.
 
• This region is famous for its pearl banks and is often referred to as the Pearl of the Indian Ocean.

 [IMAGE: https://www.worldatlas.com/r/w768/upload/fa/49/60/adobestock-516979692.jpeg]

• **Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park**

 
 
• It is a protected area in the Gulf of Mannar and covers an area of about 560 square kilometers.

• As per Article 123 of the Indian Constitution, the President has the authority to promulgate ordinances when either of the two Houses of Parliament is not in session.
 
• The ordinance holds the same force and effect as an act of Parliament.
 
• This power is intended to address urgent situations requiring immediate legislative action.

• **Ordinance:**

 
 
• An ordinance is a temporary law enacted by the President of India on the advice of the Union Cabinet.
 
• It is promulgated when Parliament is not in session and immediate action is required.
 
• Ordinances must be approved by Parliament within six weeks of reassembling, or they cease to operate.
 
• Ordinances allow the government to take swift action on matters of urgency without waiting for Parliament to convene.
 
 
 
• **Article 123 of the Indian Constitution:**
 
 
• Article 123 grants the President the power to promulgate ordinances during the recess of Parliament.
 
• This provision ensures that the executive can address urgent issues without legislative delays.
 
• Ordinances must be laid before both Houses of Parliament and require their approval to become permanent laws.
 
• This power is subject to judicial review to prevent misuse and ensure adherence to constitutional principles.
 
 
 
• **Separation of Powers:**
 
 
• The Indian Constitution follows the principle of separation of powers among the executive, legislature, and judiciary.
 
• The President's ordinance-making power represents an overlap between the executive and legislative functions.
 
• This power is exercised with checks and balances to prevent abuse and ensure accountability.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of current?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ampere**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The SI unit of electric current is the **Ampere**, symbolized as **A**.
 
• It is named after **André-Marie Ampère**, a French physicist and mathematician who is considered one of the founders of the science of classical electromagnetism.
 
• One Ampere is defined as the flow of one coulomb of charge per second.
 
• It is a fundamental unit in the International System of Units (SI), and it is used to quantify the amount of electric charge passing a point in an electric circuit per unit time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ohm (Ω)**

 
 
• The Ohm is the SI unit of electrical resistance.
 
• Named after German physicist Georg Simon Ohm, it quantifies the resistance in a circuit.
 
• One Ohm is defined as the resistance between two points of a conductor when a constant potential difference of 1 Volt, applied to these points, produces a current of 1 Ampere.
 
 
 
• **Volt (V)**
 
 
• The Volt is the SI unit of electric potential, electric potential difference, and electromotive force.
 
• Named after the Italian physicist Alessandro Volta, it measures the potential difference between two points.
 
• One Volt is defined as the potential difference that will drive one Ampere of current against one Ohm of resistance.
 
 
 
• **Metre (m)**
 
 
• The Metre is the SI unit of length.
 
• It is defined as the distance traveled by light in a vacuum in 1/299,792,458 seconds.
 
• It is a fundamental unit in the metric system and is used to measure distance.

questions.question: Name a common electrolyte disorder that occurs when the amount of sodium in your blood becomes abnormally low.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hyponatremia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Hyponatremia is a condition where the sodium level in the blood is lower than normal.
 
• Sodium is an essential electrolyte that helps regulate water balance in and around cells.
 
• Common causes of hyponatremia include excessive fluid intake, certain medications, and conditions like heart failure or kidney disease.
 
• Symptoms of hyponatremia can range from mild (nausea, headache) to severe (confusion, seizures, coma).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hyperkalemia**

 
 
• Hyperkalemia is a condition characterized by an abnormally high level of potassium in the blood.
 
• Potassium is crucial for normal cell function, especially in the heart, muscles, and nerves.
 
• Causes include kidney dysfunction, excessive potassium intake, and certain medications.
 
• Symptoms can include muscle fatigue, weakness, paralysis, and abnormal heart rhythms.
 
 
 
• **Hypokalemia**
 
 
• Hypokalemia is a condition where there is a lower than normal level of potassium in the blood.
 
• It can result from conditions like chronic kidney disease, excessive loss of potassium through urine, or inadequate potassium intake.
 
• Symptoms may include muscle cramps, weakness, fatigue, and cardiac arrhythmias.
 
• Treatment typically involves potassium supplements and addressing the underlying cause.
 
 
 
• **Hypernatremia**
 
 
• Hypernatremia is a condition where the sodium level in the blood is higher than normal.
 
• It often occurs due to dehydration, water loss, or excessive sodium intake.
 
• Symptoms can include thirst, confusion, muscle twitching, and, in severe cases, seizures or coma.
 
• Treatment focuses on slowly rehydrating the patient and addressing the cause of the sodium imbalance.

questions.question: A boatman rows to a place 30 km distant and back in 14 hours. He finds that he can row 10 km with the stream at the same time as 4 km against the stream. Find the speed (in km/h) of the stream.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Downstream speed (D) : Upstream speed (U) = Distance Ratio (in same time) = 10 : 4 = 5 : 2.

Let D = 5k and U = 2k. Total time = (30 ÷ 5k) + (30 ÷ 2k) = 14 ⇒ 6/k + 15/k = 14 ⇒ 21/k = 14 ⇒ k = 3/2.

Speed of stream = (D − U) ÷ 2 = (5k − 2k) ÷ 2 = 3k/2.

Substitute k = 3/2 ⇒ Speed of stream = (3 × 3/2) ÷ 2 = 9/4 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 9/4 km/h.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance for a one-way trip = 30 km.

Total time for the round trip = 14 hours.

Distance covered downstream in a given time = 10 km.

Distance covered upstream in the same time = 4 km.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3f50fad3d3aaed4e02ff02c8444806259d24dabbe910eafef567c9708eb33a04.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Speed of stream = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2

**Calculations:**

Let the speed of the boat in still water be u km/h and the speed of the stream be v km/h.

⇒ Downstream speed (D) = u + v

⇒ Upstream speed (U) = u − v

Since the time taken is the same for 10 km downstream and 4 km upstream:

⇒ 10 ÷ (u + v) = 4 ÷ (u − v)

⇒ (u + v) ÷ (u − v) = 10/4 = 5/2

Let Downstream speed D = 5k and Upstream speed U = 2k.

Total time taken for the round trip is 14 hours:

⇒ 30 ÷ D + 30 ÷ U = 14

⇒ 30 ÷ 5k + 30 ÷ 2k = 14

⇒ 6/k + 15/k = 14

⇒ 21/k = 14

⇒ k = 21 ÷ 14 = 3/2

Now, calculate the absolute speeds D and U:

⇒ Downstream Speed (D) = 5 × 3/2 = 15/2 = 7.5 km/h

⇒ Upstream Speed (U) = 2 × 3/2 = 3 km/h

Speed of the stream (v) = (D − U) ÷ 2

⇒ v = (7.5 − 3) ÷ 2 = 4.5 ÷ 2 = 9/4 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 9/4 km/h.**

**__Additional Information__**

Downstream and Upstream Speeds

When a boat moves with the stream, its effective speed increases (D = u + v). When it moves against the stream, its effective speed decreases (U = u − v).

Boat in Still Water

The speed of a boat in still water (u) can be calculated directly if downstream and upstream speeds are known: u = (D + U) ÷ 2.

Speed of the Stream

The speed of the stream or current (v) is half the difference between the downstream and upstream speeds: v = (D − U) ÷ 2.

Constant Time Principle

If the time taken to travel two different distances is the same, the ratio of the distances is directly proportional to the ratio of their respective speeds (D₁ ÷ D₂ = S₁ ÷ S₂).
</p

questions.question: Find the remainder: (17¹³ - 21) div 18
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

17 ÷ 18 gives a remainder of −1, so 17¹³ ÷ 18 gives a remainder of (−1)¹³ = −1.

21 ÷ 18 gives a remainder of 3.

Combined remainder = −1 − 3 = −4.

Since the remainder is negative, add the divisor: 18 − 4 = 14.

**∴ The correct answer is 14.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: (17¹³ − 21) ÷ 18

**Concept Used:**

Remainder Theorem: When dividing a polynomial by (x − a), the remainder is found by evaluating the expression at x = a.

**Calculations:**

⇒ We can express the base 17 as (18 − 1).

⇒ The given expression becomes: ((18 − 1)¹³ − 21) ÷ 18

⇒ When expanding (18 − 1)¹³ using the binomial theorem, all terms containing 18 are perfectly divisible by 18.

⇒ The only remaining term from the expansion is the constant term: (−1)¹³ = −1.

⇒ Now, divide the constant 21 by 18, which gives a remainder of 3.

⇒ Total remainder expression = −1 − 3 = −4.

⇒ A remainder of −4 means the value is 4 less than the divisor.

⇒ Actual positive remainder = 18 − 4 = 14.

**∴ The correct answer is 14.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Remainder of aⁿ ÷ (a+1)

When aⁿ is divided by (a+1), the remainder is 1 if n is an even number, and the remainder is 'a' (or −1) if n is an odd number.

Remainder of aⁿ ÷ (a−1)

When aⁿ is divided by (a−1), the remainder is always 1, regardless of whether the power n is odd or even.

Negative Remainder Concept

A negative remainder mathematically indicates how much less the number is from the next multiple of the divisor. The actual positive remainder is obtained by adding the divisor: Actual Remainder = Divisor − Negative Remainder.
</p

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

We know the standard algebraic identity: (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab.

By reversing the terms, we get: (a − b)² − (a + b)² = −4ab.

Substitute a = g and b = h directly into the given expression.

⇒ (g − h)² − (g + h)² + 4gh = −4gh + 4gh = 0.

Expression: (g − h)² − (g + h)² + 4gh

(a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

**Calculations:**

Expand the first term (g − h)²:

⇒ g² + h² − 2gh

Expand the second term (g + h)²:

⇒ g² + h² + 2gh

Substitute both expansions back into the original expression:

⇒ (g² + h² − 2gh) − (g² + h² + 2gh) + 4gh

Distribute the negative sign over the second term:

⇒ g² + h² − 2gh − g² − h² − 2gh + 4gh

Group the like terms together:

⇒ (g² − g²) + (h² − h²) − 2gh − 2gh + 4gh

⇒ 0 + 0 − 4gh + 4gh

⇒ 0

The difference between the squares of two terms can be factored into a product: a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b).

When the arc length and radius of a sector are given, its area can be found directly using the formula:

Area = ½ × l × r

questions.question: Kalyan spends 80% of his income. His income increases by 15% and his expenditure also increases by 5%. The percentage of increase in his savings is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Expenditure to Savings = 80% : 20% = 4 : 1.

We apply the weighted average method: Income = Expenditure + Savings.

Change in Income = (Exp Ratio × Exp Change + Sav Ratio × Sav Change) ÷ Total Ratio

⇒ 15% = (4 × 5% + 1 × x%) ÷ 5

⇒ 75% = 20% + x% ⇒ x = 55%

**∴ The correct answer is 55%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Kalyan spends 80% of his income.

Increase in income = 15%.

Increase in expenditure = 5%.

**Formula Used:**

Savings = Income − Expenditure

Percentage Increase = (Increase Value ÷ Initial Value) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fe676e11c7b5cc88f9a98caef9fe4134c499afdb29816b38ac73b3bde9d5d14f.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let initial income be 100 units.

⇒ Initial expenditure = 80% of 100 = 80 units

⇒ Initial savings = 100 − 80 = 20 units

⇒ After a 15% increase, new income = 100 + 15 = 115 units

⇒ After a 5% increase, new expenditure = 80 + (5% of 80) = 80 + 4 = 84 units

⇒ New savings = New income − New expenditure = 115 − 84 = 31 units

⇒ Increase in savings = 31 − 20 = 11 units

⇒ Percentage increase in savings = (11 ÷ 20) × 100 = 55%

**∴ The correct answer is 55%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income, Expenditure & Savings

The basic relationship is Income = Expenditure + Savings. Any percentage change in income impacts both expenditure and savings proportional to their initial distributions.

Percentage Change Formula

Profit % = [(24 − 19) / 19] × 100 = 5/19 × 100 = 500/19 %

First term = 2(2 + √3) + 2(2 − √3) = 8.

⇒ = cosecA × [ (cosecA + 1 + cosecA − 1) ÷ (cosec²A − 1) ]

⇒ = 2(1/cos²A) ÷ (sin²A/cos²A) = 2/sin²A = 2cosec²A

⇒ Substitute both simplified parts into the original expression:

⇒ Result = 2sec²A × (2cosec²A)−¹ = 2sec²A ÷ 2cosec²A

⇒ Result = (1/cos²A) ÷ (1/sin²A) = sin²A ÷ cos²A = tan²A

⇒ Given A = 60°, substitute the value:

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

questions.question: 2 biscuits and 1 chocolate cost ₹69. 2 chocolates and 3 cups of coffee cost ₹127. 3 biscuits, 4 chocolates and 2 cups of coffee cost ₹229. Find the total cost (in ₹) of 5 biscuits, 5 chocolates and 5 cups of coffee.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let b, c, and f be the unit prices of biscuit, chocolate, and coffee.

Given: 2b + c = 69; 2c + 3f = 127; 3b + 4c + 2f = 229.

From the first, c = 69 − 2b. Substitute this in the other two equations:

4b − 3f = 11 and 5b − 2f = 47. Solving these gives b = 17, f = 19.

Hence, c = 69 − 2(17) = 35. Total cost of 1 set = 17 + 35 + 19 = 71.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹355.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Let the cost of 1 biscuit, 1 chocolate, and 1 coffee be b, c, and f respectively.

Given:

⇒ 2b + c = 69 --- (1)

⇒ 2c + 3f = 127 --- (2)

⇒ 3b + 4c + 2f = 229 --- (3)

From (1), we get c = 69 − 2b.

Substitute c in (2):

⇒ 2(69 − 2b) + 3f = 127

⇒ 138 − 4b + 3f = 127

⇒ 4b − 3f = 11 --- (4)

Substitute c in (3):

⇒ 3b + 4(69 − 2b) + 2f = 229

⇒ 3b + 276 − 8b + 2f = 229

⇒ 5b − 2f = 47 --- (5)

Multiply (4) by 2 and (5) by 3:

⇒ 8b − 6f = 22

⇒ 15b − 6f = 141

Subtracting the first equation from the second:

⇒ 7b = 119 ⇒ b = 17

Putting b = 17 in (1):

⇒ 2(17) + c = 69 ⇒ c = 69 − 34 = 35

Putting c = 35 in (2):

⇒ 2(35) + 3f = 127 ⇒ 3f = 127 − 70 = 57 ⇒ f = 19

Total cost of 5 of each item = 5 × (b + c + f)

⇒ 5 × (17 + 35 + 19) = 5 × 71 = 355

**∴ The correct answer is ₹355.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**
